text:
Droit de la famille — 212670

2021 QCCS 5830

SUPERIOR COURT

(Family Division)

CANADA

PROVINCE OF
QUEBEC

DISTRICT OF

MONTREAL

No:

500-12-308000-110

DATE:

July 8,
2021

______________________________________________________________________

BY

THE
HONOURABLE

JEFFREY EDWARDS,
J.S.C.

______________________________________________________________________

S. K.

Plaintiff

v.

A. S.

Defendant

______________________________________________________________________

JUDGMENT
ON CHOICE OF HIGH SCHOOL

(Transcript
of an oral judgment
[1]
)

______________________________________________________________________

[
1
]

CONSIDERING
that Xis twelve (12) years old and that she has
been brought up in the Jewish faith;

[
2
]

CONSIDERING
that A. S. (
Father
) identifies as being
of the Jewish faith and favours that X attend a high school which provides an
immersive environment in Jewish culture, values and traditions while respecting
and conforming to the education curriculum prescribed by the Quebec Ministry of
Education;

[
3
]

CONSIDERING
that S. K. (
Mother
) also identifies as
being of the Jewish faith but favours the choice of a secular school for X and
prefers that exposure and learning of Jewish culture, values and traditions
take place outside of the normal school program, such as after-school, family
and community activities;

[
4
]

CONSIDERING
that X has attended a secular school from
kindergarten to grade six (6) (School A);

[
5
]

CONSIDERING
that, according to the evidence, X is bright,
mature, thoughtful, curious and succeeds extremely well in both educational and
social settings;

[
6
]

CONSIDERING
that X has undertaken her own research on the
Internet, attended virtual open houses of various high schools and spoken to
friends about their high school choices and experiences;

[
7
]

CONSIDERING
that X has applied to several high schools and
been accepted to all of them;

[
8
]

CONSIDERING
that X’s first choice is School B. This school
is also favoured by the Father in light of his preference as expressed above
for an enhanced education of Jewish culture, values and traditions in a school
setting;

[
9
]

CONSIDERING
that X’s second choice is [School C]. That
school is favoured by the Mother in light of her preference, as expressed
above, for an education for her daughter in a secular school setting;

[
10
]

CONSIDERING
the judgment of
the Quebec Court of Appeal in
Droit
de la famille — 201310
[2]

which held that from the age of twelve (12) and older, the minor child’s
preferences and articulated opinion on school choice should be respected and is
determinative, unless the Court is of the view that it is not in the best
interest of the child to do so. The Court of Appeal also instructs the trial
judge to verify whether the choice expressed by the child is appropriate for her
and that the reasons expressed by the child in support of the choice are
rational;

[
11
]

According to the
representations conveyed to the Court on behalf of X by a Court-appointed
attorney, X’s preference is for School B. According to the letter filed by her
attorney, which summarizes X’s reasons and which letter has been approved by X,
her choice and preference are based on her desire to explore and intensify her
Jewish faith and her personal belonging to the Jewish religion, and to better
know the culture, values, traditions, customs and perspectives of the Jewish
faith;

[
12
]

X stated to her attorney
[3]
:

“There
is not a lot of Judaism in the world and I need to remember how special it is.”

[
13
]

According to X’s attorney, her
client is very interested in learning more about her Jewish faith. According to
the letter approved by X, she ranks School B higher than [School C] because of
the religious education which she feels she has been missing.

[
14
]

X is also of the view that School
B is a bit warmer in its approach and that the teachers appear to be very
enthusiastic and happy. She also states that she needs to learn to adapt to
different systems and that School B will offer the diversity that she is seeking.

[
15
]

The Mother is concerned that
X has been unduly influenced by the Father and that X’s preference is motivated
by her desire to please him. The Father attended School B
[4]
. After review of
the evidence, the Court sees no proof of undue pressure.

[
16
]

The Mother is also concerned
that X is not adequately prepared for certain special courses, such as Hebrew,
since most of the School B students have covered these subjects from the
beginning of elementary school. However, School B offers an accelerated program
in Grades 7 and 8 (Secondary 1 and 2) in these areas so that by Grade 9 (Secondary
3), all of the school’s students are at a similar knowledge level in these
areas. X is aware of this issue and, according to the letter approved by her, she
looks forward to this challenge and the opportunity to make friends in similar
circumstances. Furthermore, the accelerated program is only offered in Grades 7
and 8, so now would be the appropriate time for X to register for School B.

[
17
]

The Mother also prefers the
stability of a secular school environment, such as the one experienced by X at School
A and the one offered by [School C]. However, X has considered these factors, as
well as what appear to be superior athletic facilities at [School C]. Nevertheless,
X makes known to the Court, through her attorney, that it is more important for
her to become more aware about and to develop her Jewish identity.

[
18
]

Both the Mother and the
Father agree that X is a bright, thoughtful and a mature young woman. The Court
is of the view that X’s choice of School B is an entirely appropriate one for
her and that the reasons provided by her to support that choice are rational.

[
19
]

The Court concludes that X’s
preference and choice should be respected. In light of the fact that X has
expressed a distinct preference for School B, the Court is of the view that it
is in the best interest of X to respect her choice to explore and learn in a
school setting where Jewish culture, values, traditions, customs and beliefs are
more present than they would be in a secular school setting.

[
20
]

There is every reason to
hope and expect that X will be satisfied and content at School B. Should that
not be the case, X can express that view to her parents. In such circumstances,
if X requests a change of high school, the parents can review the options at
that time, notably in light of a preference expressed by X. In such event, failing
agreement of the parents, either parent may apply to the Court for a decision
in that regard.

FOR THESE REASONS, THE COURT:

[
21
]

ORDERS
that the minor child X be enrolled and attend
at School B for the start of the 2021-2022 school year;

[
22
]

ORDERS
that the parties support their daughter to
integrate into that school;

[
23
]

DECLARE
that all costs related to the minor child’s
education at School B are special expenses, including those for tuition,
uniforms and school supplies;

[
24
]

THE WHOLE WITHOUT COSTS
.

JEFFREY
EDWARDS, J.S.C.
